title: Count of Integers
summary: Given numeric strings num1 and num2, along with integers max_sum and min_sum, find the count of integers x that satisfy num1 <= x <= num2 and min_sum <= digit_sum(x) <= max_sum.
statement: Given numeric strings num1 and num2, along with integers max_sum and min_sum, find the count of integers x that satisfy num1 <= x <= num2 and min_sum <= digit_sum(x) <= max_sum. Return the count modulo 10^9 + 7, where digit_sum(x) is the sum of the digits of x.
constraints: Consider every integer in the inclusive decimal range num1 through num2.
Count values whose decimal digit sum lies between min_sum and max_sum inclusive.
hints: Write a helper that counts qualifying integers from zero through one bound.
Digit DP state stores position, accumulated digit sum, and whether the prefix still equals the bound.
Subtract count(num1-1) from count(num2), reducing modulo the required constant.
Every bounded decimal representation follows exactly one DP digit path, and the terminal range check accepts precisely the desired digit sums.
editorial: Every bounded decimal representation follows exactly one DP digit path, and the terminal range check accepts precisely the desired digit sums.

tests.explanation: Every value except nine has digit sum at most eight, so eleven values qualify.
Only the endpoint five has digit sum exactly five.
